title: Reliability initiative: Continuous validation & rollout gating playbook
creator: Asha Menon
description: Create a repeatable, cross-team playbook and initiative-tracker artifact for continuous validation tied to reliability objectives. The goal is to operationalize: 1) automated canary validations driven by synthetic traffic and real-user sampling, 2) error-budget-aware rollout gates (burn-rate and SLI drift triggers), and 3) a compact decision log and handoff flow for reallocating initiative runway. This ticket captures the PM playbook, acceptance criteria, dashboards to build, owners for each step, and the comms plan for scaled rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step runbook and owner matrix
Automated canary pipeline templates (CI job + synthetic runner) added to repo
Dashboard: per-initiative SLI trend + burn-rate with 1h/6h/24h rollups available
Rollout gating rules codified and can be toggled per-release (canary size, burn-rate thresholds, auto-rollback)
Two pilot rollouts completed (one hosted API change, one Dedicated config change) demonstrating gate behavior
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Chose synthetic + sampled real traffic hybrid for canaries to reduce false positives from synthetic-only tests

2026-02-18: Decided on three-bucket burn-rate gating: green (<10% projected), amber (10-30% projected, pause and investigate), red (>30% projected, auto-rollback). Trade-off: more aggressive rollbacks reduce uptime risk but increase flapping for transient telemetry anomalies.

2026-02-25: Opted to integrate canary results with existing rollout service instead of building a new orchestration layer to accelerate MVP; engineering noted additional work to map model variants to rollout keys.
2026-03-04: Deferred per-customer error-budget reallocation to a follow-up (privacy/contract work), will surface manual override in Console for enterprise customers
